question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: Reading the SIG. FIXED = the number of parameters not marked rest. REST = the type of the FIRST parameter marked rest; a rest parameter with no type (absent or none) means there is NO rest. Argument j (0-based) is wired at the type of the j-th entry of the WHOLE parameter list when j < FIXED (whether or not that entry is the rest one), else at REST. CITED FIDELITY package

Throws, and only these, before any argument is looked at: sig is none or absent, sig has no parameter list (or one that is not a list), or a parameter entry is none. They throw even when args is malformed. Nothing else throws (R5).

Shape. args not a list -> NARROWED "the args are not a list". No REST and the args count differs from FIXED -> NARROWED "<count> args for a <FIXED>-parameter SIG". With a REST any count passes, fewer than FIXED included (only the arguments present are wired). Then, before any argument is wired, a hole anywhere in args -> NARROWED HOLE_TEXT (it wins over every argument's own result, faults included). CITED FIDELITY package

Walk. The arguments are wired left to right by WIRE (R6-R16); the FIRST argument whose wire is NARROWED is the result and no later argument is examined. Otherwise the result is "[" + the wires joined by "," + "]"; no arguments -> "[]".

A host fault while wiring one argument (a malformed type node, TABLE MALFORMED) -> NARROWED "wire: " + the fault message. Inside one list, tuple or record EVERY element / item / field is wired before the first NARROWED among them is chosen, so a fault anywhere inside an argument wins over a NARROWED sibling in it; across arguments R4's order decides.

None and absent first, at every typed position, any depth. The ABSENT value (an argument, list element or tuple item that is absent, or a declared record field the value lacks or holds as absent) is tested FIRST, by reading the node: at a none node or an OPTION union (R7) it wires "null"; at every other node (json, map, a multi-way union, a scalar, a kind outside the set, a node with no k) -> NARROWED ABSENT_REASON. Then a none value wires "null" before the type is read, whatever the type (malformed included). So on a malformed node absent can fault (TABLE MALFORMED) where none cannot. CITED FIDELITY package

Union. An OPTION union — exactly two alternatives, exactly one of them not none, in either order — wires the value by that alternative's rule. Every other union (two non-none alternatives, three or more, one, or zero) wires the value by the json rule R15, whatever the alternatives are: the value is never checked against them. CITED FIDELITY package

f64. A number -> its IEEE-754 binary64 bit pattern as a JSON string of exactly 16 lowercase hex digits, every NaN as 7ff8000000000000 (-0 -> "8000000000000000", +Infinity -> "7ff0000000000000"). Anything else (a big integer included) -> NARROWED "not an f64 value".
text. A text with a lone surrogate -> NARROWED "a lone surrogate has no UTF-8 form"; another text -> TEXT-ESCAPE. Anything else (a boxed text included) -> NARROWED "not a text value".
bool. true / false -> "true" / "false"; anything else -> NARROWED "not a bool value".

i64 and u64. Accepted: a big integer, or a number that is an integer of magnitude at most 2^53-1 (-0 counts, and is 0); in range [-2^63, 2^63-1] for i64, [0, 2^64-1] for u64 -> its exact decimal digits ("-" when negative). Anything else (a fraction, 2^53 as a number, out of range, non-number) -> NARROWED "not a i64 value" / "not a u64 value". CITED FIDELITY package

list. Not a list (a byte array, a text, a map: anything but a list) -> NARROWED "not a list value". A list with any hole -> NARROWED HOLE_TEXT (checked before any element is wired). Otherwise each element is wired at the item type; the first NARROWED element is the wire; else "[" + the element wires joined by "," + "]".

tuple. A list with any hole -> NARROWED HOLE_TEXT, checked first (before the length test and before the node's items are read, so it wins over a wrong length and over a node with no items). Otherwise: not a list, or a list whose length differs from the item count -> NARROWED "not a <items>-tuple"; else item i is wired at item type i, first NARROWED wins, else "[...]" as R12. CITED FIDELITY package

record. Not a plain map (a list, keyed collection, set, byte array, regexp, boxed value, scalar) -> NARROWED "not a record value". Otherwise each declared field, in declared order, wires the value's OWN property of that name at the field type — a missing one is absent (R6: "null" only at a none or option field; an inherited member such as constructor is never read). First NARROWED field wins; else "{" + each JSON-quoted field name (TEXT-ESCAPE) + ":" + its wire, joined by ",", + "}". Undeclared keys of the value are dropped unchecked.

json and map (and R7's non-option unions). If the value is NOT CARRIABLE -> NARROWED with the first REASON found by CARRY; otherwise the value's PLAIN rendering. A map position never consults its key or value type: map[text, f64] holding "x" sends "x", a number as decimal (not bits). CARRY, depth first, elements in index order and map entries in HOST KEY ORDER (a key before its value): none, bool -> carriable; a number that is NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity or -0 -> NARROWED_JSON; a whole number of magnitude above 2^53 (2^53 itself passes) -> "a whole number past 2^53 reaches serde_json as a different integer" (whether or not its rendering would be exact); a big integer below -2^63 or above 2^64-1 -> "an integer past i64/u64 has no serde_json form"; a text (or a map key) with a lone surrogate -> "a lone surrogate has no UTF-8 form"; the absent value (nested) -> ABSENT_REASON; a list hole -> HOLE_TEXT; a plain map -> its entries; a list -> its elements; any other object -> "a <TAG> has no serde_json form", TAG = the host's class name: Uint8Array (a host byte buffer too), Map (keyed collection), Set, RegExp, Number, String, Boolean (boxed). CITED FIDELITY package

Every other kind (bytes, none, a kind outside the closed set, a node with no k) -> NARROWED "the rust harness has no route for <k>", <k> the kind text as written, or ABSENT_TEXT when the node has no k. CITED FIDELITY package

PLAIN rendering (only of CARRIABLE values): a big integer -> its decimal digits, unquoted; none -> "null"; bool -> "true" / "false"; a number -> NUMBER-TEXT (CARRY has removed every whole number past 2^53); text -> TEXT-ESCAPE; a list -> "[" + elements PLAIN joined by "," + "]"; a plain map -> "{" + each TEXT-ESCAPE key + ":" + value PLAIN, joined by ",", + "}" in HOST KEY ORDER: keys that are array indices (the canonical decimal spelling of an integer 0 .. 2^32-2) first, ascending numerically, then every other key in creation order. CITED FIDELITY package
the type node itself is missing or none, any value but none (absent included)     -> Cannot read properties of <x> (reading 'k')
a union node with no alts, any value but none (absent included)                   -> Cannot read properties of <x> (reading 'filter')
a list node with no item, at an element that is not none (absent included)        -> Cannot read properties of <x> (reading 'k')
a tuple node with no items, a present value that is not a list with a hole        -> Cannot read properties of <x> (reading 'length')
a record node with no fields, the value a plain map                               -> Cannot read properties of <x> (reading 'map')
U+0022 quotation mark                                -> ESC then the quotation mark
U+005C reverse solidus                               -> ESC then ESC
U+0008 U+0009 U+000A U+000C U+000D                   -> ESC then the letter b, t, n, f, r respectively
any other unit below U+0020                          -> ESC, the letter u, "00", two lowercase hex digits
everything else (U+007F, U+2028, U+2029, a surrogate pair) -> itself, unescaped
k <= n <= 21                     -> the digits followed by n-k zeros
0 < n <= 21                      -> the first n digits, ".", the rest
-6 < n <= 0                      -> "0." then -n zeros then the digits
otherwise                        -> d[.ddd] then "e", then "+" or "-", then abs(n-1) (1e+21, 1e-7, 1.5e-7)
